title: Eye, Ear, Mouth, and Nose
label: ch:pa-face-parts
canDo: I can name the eye, ear, mouth, and nose in Punjabi, tell a doubled consonant that survived from one that vanished into tone, and clear up the false friend ਕੰਨ shares in spelling, but not in root, with ਕਰਨਾ.

payoff.summary: The chapter closes on ਨੱਕ, completing the face: the reader produces ਅੱਖ, ਕੰਨ, ਮੂੰਹ and ਨੱਕ, names ਅੱਖ and ਨੱਕ as unbroken PIE cousins of eye and nose that kept their doubled consonants and so never traded a sound for a tone, and states that ਮੂੰਹ alone among the four carries a level high tone, the same one first heard in ਚਾਹ.
